label: Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B
params_summary: 2.4T total / 95B active · 92 layers · hybrid linear attention + 512-expert MoE
notes: ADDED 2026-08-21 as the second member of the Qwen3.8 family. The client's model page splits Qwen by generation now, which made the answer to 'what else is in 3.8?' visible: Qwen ships exactly two 3.8 models, this one and the 27B. Everything under 'Qwen3.8-9B' / 'Qwen3.8-4B' on Hugging Face is a third-party distillation, not a Qwen release, so it is not in the catalogue.

⚠ THE ONBOARDING GATE OF HARD CONSTRAINT #2 HAS NOT RUN. No ppl band, no testbed smoke: the smallest published precision is 370 GiB and the four testbed machines pool ~150 GiB, so neither is possible here — not 'not done yet', but not doable on this hardware. It is listed available=true on the same footing as GLM-5.2 (202 GiB) and DeepSeek V4 Pro (530 GiB), which are in the catalogue under the same limitation. If that precedent is wrong it is wrong for all three, and this note is where the argument starts.

Architecture: general.architecture = 'qwen35moe' — the same architecture as qwen3.5-35b-a3b, which HAS been verified against llama.cpp on real weights. Every geometry field was read from this model's own GGUF header (scripts/measure_gguf.py --meta on UD-Q1_0): block_count 93, embedding_length 8192, 64 q heads / 4 KV heads x 256, full_attention_interval 4, ssm inner 16384 / state 128 / group 16 / conv 4, expert_count 512, expert_used_count 10, vocab 248320, ctx 262144, rope base 1e7.

MTP / n_layers: qwen35moe.block_count is 93 and qwen35moe.nextn_predict_layers is 1, so block 92 is an MTP (NextN) draft head, not a decode layer — n_layers is 92. Same relationship as qwen3.8-27b, whose header says block_count 65 / nextn 1 against n_layers 64; that pair was used as the positive control for reading this one. Counting the MTP block as a decode layer would mis-size every node in the split.

KV numbers are DERIVED from the header, not measured on a loaded model. Full layers: 2 (K+V) x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 4 B = 8192 B/token/layer. Linear layers: v_heads(128) x v_dim(128) x k_dim(128) x 4 B for the recurrent state, plus (conv_kernel-1)=3 x (2 x k_heads x k_dim + ssm_inner = 20480) x 4 B for the conv window = 8,634,368 B, context-independent. The formula is not invented for this model: applied to qwen3.5-35b-a3b it reproduces 4096 / 2,195,456 and to qwen3.8-27b 8192 / 3,268,608 — both exactly, and both of those were measured independently. That is the positive control on the derivation; it is still a derivation.

layer_weight_bytes carries the WHOLE file size and shared_weight_bytes is 0 — the same convention as every other manifest here (the planner only uses their sum, and shared_weight_bytes is charged to every node, which would over-count a cluster).

Source: unsloth/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-GGUF. Nine precisions, 370 GiB (UD-Q1_0) to 4557 GiB (BF16). Every byte count, sha256 and revision comes from the HF API and from HTTP Range reads of the file headers — no weights were downloaded to the control machine.

LICENSE IS NOT APACHE-2.0. The 27B is; this one is Qwen's own 'qwen3.8-max' licence (cardData license_name on Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, text in that repo's LICENSE file). Worth a read before it is offered through the marketplace, because that is redistribution-adjacent in a way running it at home is not.

Thinking model, like the 27B: the chat template turns reasoning on by default at 'xhigh' effort. The sidecar's `--reasoning off` default covers the known failure mode (the whole max_tokens burnt inside <think>).
The GGUF carries the publisher's sampling recommendation: temp 1.0, top_k 20, top_p 0.95.
